title: Magehold Wanderlight - Cozy walking harvesting tower defense adventure!
author: MosskeepForest
selftext:
Finally got my new game Wanderlight up with a steam page! [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5524750/Magehold\_Wanderlight/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5524750/Magehold_Wanderlight/) 

This is a related game to my previous game Magehold Fairwinds ( [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5353860/Magehold\_Fairwinds/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5353860/Magehold_Fairwinds/) ) but plays very differently.

Wanderlight is my first dive into a proper 3d game too. More RTS (so the quirky character models aren't a problem), gathering materials and building defenses, and just a cozy adventure across the world defending at night.

For a lot of my character models, I had claude make them in blender (after trying to do them just programatically). It was a little bit of an upgrade with blender, but honestly not THAT much. 

What was a bigger boost in quality was redoing all of the environment textures with the help of GPT. And then keep pushing it for better environment areas (building a lava area now). 

But, yea, most of it is really just the game design and handing it off and then testing and playing it and seeing what else it needs. It was able to take the idea for the platforms and buildings and everything and just run with it. 

Same with dungeons, just grabbed the idea and went. 

Animations need checking though (from bad weight painting). Having it throw out GIFs for approval on those and effects helps a lot to check through a lot of different characters / places quickly. 

Overall, I think probably this 3d game had a bit slower dev time than the 2d game. Getting them climbing the ladder up into the ship, or the platform, those took a few tries. But yelling at it helped.

And that's really the workflow. Test, make a list of what's off, and throw it your bug / issue reports for another pass. Do that until you got what you want.
